txt_2:
In this experiment, you will be choosing between two given images. Before making your choice, you will be provided with information of other participants and their choices of the same images. Your choice of the images will determine your final payment.
Press SPACE to continue

txt: Before making your choice, you will be provided with information about other participants who previously were learning about the same two images. This information includes participant's political orientation and IQ. You will first be shown an overview of multiple participants at the same time.
txt_2:
Before the experiment begins, you will view information about other participants who previously completed the same experiment.
Each participant is represented by a distinct geometric symbol.

Press SPACE to continue.

txt: Political orientation will be shown as their responses to the political questions they answered before taking part in the experiment. Your responses will also be indicated.
txt_2:
The first piece of information about the other participants will be their political orientation, shown as their responses to the political questions they answered before taking part in the experiment. This will be presented once for all participants before the experiment begins.

Press SPACE to continue

txt: You will also be given each participant's IQ information.
txt_2:
You will also be given each participant's IQ information.
The information will be presented once for all participants before the experiment begins

Press SPACE to continue.

txt: After that, you will be noted with which participant you will be observing choices from.
txt_2:
Before observing the choices of a particular participant, their information will be presented again in bold. 

Press SPACE to continue.

txt: That participant's information (political orientation & IQ) will be presented again individually in bold.
txt_2:
You may use both information to predict the participant's choices and to inform your own choices.

Press SPACE to continue

txt: That participant's information (IQ) will be presented again individually in bold.
txt_2:
Once you have reviewed the participant information, please rate how well you expect each participant to perform in this experiment, using a scale from 0 to 100.
This rating will be made twice for each participant: once immediately after you review the participant information, and once again after trials are complete.

Press SPACE to continue.

txt:
Next, you will be asked to indicate how close you feel to the participant.
Use the scale ranging from 0 (Not close at all) to 100 (Very close) to rate your overall sense of closeness to them.

txt_2:
You will now observe the past choices made by this specific participant as they tried to learn which of the two images was more rewarding. Please keep in mind that not all participants learned equally well.

Before you are shown what the other person actually chose, you must first predict what you think they selected. You can then decide how best to use their choice to guide your own decision and maximize your payoff.

Note: In the very first round, you will not have seen any of the other person's decisions yet. Therefore, your first prediction will simply be a random guess.

txt:
A round then proceeds as follows:

1. Predict what the other participant will choose
2. Observe what they actually choose
3. Make your own choice

To view a round, press the <Space> key.
txt_2:
A round then proceeds as follows:

First, you will see the other person and you should predict the image that the other person has chosen. In the beginning, you should guess to predict the other’s choice, but after few rounds, you will have an idea what they will choose.

Then, it will be shown which image the person actually selected.
Next, you choose one of the same two images yourself. Note that the position of the images can vary between the other person and you and only the identity matters for determining which image has higher probability of reward.

To view a round, press the <Space> key.
